summary: 54-year-old man, 2 days of LIF pain, T 37.8 °C, tolerating oral intake, WBC 12.4, CRP 88; CT: uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis. Colonoscopy 3 years ago.

inputs.hpi: 2 days of constant left lower abdominal pain, mild nausea, eating and drinking. Felt warm last night. Bowels opened normally. Colonoscopy 3 years ago showed sigmoid diverticular disease only. Otherwise fit, no immunosuppression.

exam.abdomen: Tenderness in the left iliac fossa, no guarding elsewhere, no mass, no peritonism.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Sigmoid diverticulitis with pericolic fat stranding. No abscess, no extraluminal gas, no free fluid (uncomplicated).

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute uncomplicated diverticulitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Uncomplicated acute sigmoid diverticulitis (CT-confirmed), immunocompetent, tolerating oral intake. Outpatient management; antibiotics not routinely required.

emergencyLevel.note: Same-day assessment, but an emergency redirect is over-triage for CT-confirmed uncomplicated disease in a well patient.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: iOS: ClinicalPathwayEngine reads only CC/PMH keywords; CC 'Left lower abdominal pain' gives 'routine'.

mustInclude.note: WSES 2020 / AGA 2021 / ASCRS 2020: in immunocompetent patients with mild uncomplicated diverticulitis antibiotics can be omitted (selective use); outpatient care.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: No antibiotic-free option; protocol and variant prescribe co-amoxiclav for 5–7 days.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Update the uncomplicated step to WSES 2020 / AGA 2021: antibiotics selectively; observation without antibiotics in immunocompetent patients without systemic features.

mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web: '[conservative] Uncomplicated: oral co-amoxiclav 625 mg TDS for 5–7 days' in the documented plan.

dxVariant.knownGapNote: Web: Keyword 'uncomplicated diverticulitis' is not a substring of 'Uncomplicated acute sigmoid diverticulitis'; no variant is selected.

guideline.name: WSES guidelines — acute colonic diverticulitis in the emergency setting (2020 update)
guideline.section: CT staging (WSES CT classification); uncomplicated: antibiotics not always needed in immunocompetent patients, outpatient care; abscess >4–5 cm: percutaneous drainage + antibiotics; generalised peritonitis: emergency surgery (Hartmann's or resection with primary anastomosis ± stoma); immunocompromised: high risk, antibiotics, low threshold for surgery
guideline.citation: Sartelli M, Weber DG, Kluger Y, et al. 2020 update of the WSES guidelines for the management of acute colonic diverticulitis in the emergency setting. World J Emerg Surg. 2020;15:32.

guideline.name: AGA clinical practice update — medical management of colonic diverticulitis
guideline.section: Antibiotics used selectively rather than routinely in immunocompetent patients with mild uncomplicated diverticulitis; CT when diagnosis uncertain; colonoscopy after complicated diverticulitis or if not recently done
guideline.citation: Peery AF, Shaukat A, Strate LL. AGA clinical practice update on medical management of colonic diverticulitis: expert review. Gastroenterology. 2021;160:906–11.e1.

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — left-sided colonic diverticulitis
guideline.section: Selective antibiotics for uncomplicated disease; percutaneous drainage for large abscess; urgent colectomy for diffuse peritonitis; immunocompromised patients; colonoscopy after complicated disease
guideline.citation: Hall J, Hardiman K, Lee S, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of left-sided colonic diverticulitis. Dis Colon Rectum. 2020;63:728–47.

rationale: Base case. Current guidance (WSES 2020, AGA 2021, ASCRS 2020) allows outpatient management without antibiotics in selected immunocompetent patients with uncomplicated disease.
